blocks.content:
Welcome to my blog! 👋

This is where I'll be sharing everything — posts, long-form articles, photos, videos and the occasional song. It's still early days, but I wanted to get the first post out the door.

Stick around!

Just published a new article on getting started with Flask. It walks through the whole setup from scratch — routing, templates and a tiny bit of MongoDB.

/article/article_flask_intro

Let me know what you think!

Spent the weekend wiring up media uploads. Images, video and audio all render inline now, and articles support mixed text and media blocks.

Feels good to finally publish the way I actually write.
Flask is a tiny Python web framework that gets out of your way. You can have a working site in a single file, which makes it perfect for a project like this blog.
The core ideas are simple: routes map URLs to Python functions, and Jinja templates render the HTML. Everything else — the database, file uploads, authentication — you layer on as you need it.
In this post I'll cover the setup I'm using: Flask for the app, MongoDB for storage, and a media folder for uploads. Each piece is small enough to understand on its own.
I've wanted a place of my own for a while — somewhere that isn't an algorithm deciding who sees what I write.
The goal is simple: write, publish, and let it live here. Short posts for quick thoughts, articles for the longer pieces.
Eventually I'd like to cross-post to other platforms automatically, but for now this is the home base.

published.title: Deploying a Flask App to Azure

blocks.content: Deploying a Flask app to Azure Web Apps is mostly about the right configuration. A GitHub Actions workflow builds the app, installs the requirements, and pushes it up.
The two things that trip people up: keeping secrets in application settings rather than the repo, and picking a startup command that points at your WSGI app.
Once it's wired up, every push to main ships automatically.
